claims.text: The initial material is an elemental Cr coating on a zirconium-alloy fuel-cladding substrate.
A VZrHfNbTa HEA layer is to be deposited on top of the Cr coating.
Elevated-temperature Cr-Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of the Cr coating.
The added VZrHfNbTa layer will prevent premature coating failure caused by Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Exposure of the modified coating system will form an HfZr alloy transition layer.
The HfZr transition layer will chemically combine the HEA layer with the zirconium-alloy substrate.
The VZrHfNbTa layer acts as a diffusion barrier.
The VZrHfNbTa layer reduces Cr-Zr interdiffusion relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline.
The VZrHfNbTa layer is oxidation resistant.
The VZrHfNbTa layer reduces oxide growth relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline.
The modified coating preserves protection during normal subcritical-water operation.
The modified coating preserves protection in accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
The modified coating provides better overall protection than the unmodified Cr-coated baseline.
The proposed protection remains effective at temperatures up to 1600 °C.
The proposed protection remains effective for exposure times up to 5 hours.

contradictions.description: The HEA is placed on top of the Cr coating, so the intervening Cr layer separates it from the zirconium substrate; nevertheless, the mediator is described as an HfZr layer directly combining the HEA layer and substrate.

A layer deposited above the Cr coating is not positioned at the buried Cr-Zr interface, yet it is asserted to act directly as the barrier to Cr-Zr interdiffusion without an explained transport pathway or architectural change.
